highlights.text: Benchmarks 2026: mid-market SaaS logo churn clusters at 6-8% a year across 140 private companies, with a median of 7.1%. Vendors reporting under 2% are usually quoting net revenue churn after expansion, annualizing a single good quarter, or computing logo churn after removing downgrades. Always ask which definition a deck uses, and get the logo number before discussing expansion.

Net revenue retention above 115% usually means the vendor expands inside existing accounts faster than it loses them. It says nothing about how many logos leave. Read NDR and logo churn as a pair, never alone.

Expansion masks churn on a predictable schedule: a base losing 7% of logos a year can print 115-120% NDR for years if the survivors grow seats 20% or more. The tell is gross retention. If gross retention trails the category median of 90%, the bucket is leaking no matter what NDR says.
Second meetings are for disproving the thesis, not confirming it. Go in with one number to break and one question the founders hope you will not ask.

Open with the benchmark, then let the CFO define the metric before reacting. Write down exact numbers, not adjectives. A founder who answers the definition question precisely usually has nothing to hide; a founder who reframes it is telling you where the bodies are.
